ui.note: Text people type keeps its own direction in Arabic: input and textarea fields use dir=auto, rendered notes and comments take their own direction, and titles, list and people names and label chips inside translated text are isolated so punctuation and list separators stay in place. Arabic link underlines use a larger offset. Behavior, permissions, data and keyboard shortcuts are unchanged.

release.note: Prepare fourth beta 0.1.0-beta.4/Android code 16 after the v0.1.0-beta.3 tag failed the Debian image gate and never published (its run built code 15). Releases stay Alpine and Zero only (#1267); the changelog says why the -debian image is missing. Retain signing certificate, documentation epoch, remaining prerelease/native limits and prerelease publication wording; release steps are unchanged.

configuration.noImpact: The Alpine app, Zero, all-in-one and push-relay images upgrade zlib to 1.3.2-r1 alongside the existing targeted package upgrades; no settings, defaults or formats change.

deployment.noImpact: Images now carry zlib 1.3.2-r1 (CVE-2026-85091); bases, tags, entrypoints and upgrade steps are unchanged, so deployments need no action beyond pulling new images.

native.note: Refuse Capacitor file, content and HTTP proxy resources for every WebView request, clear exported Activity task affinity and explicitly exclude native session and push preferences from Android cloud backup and device transfer. Preserve the release-only manifest guard and trusted-server choice of HTTPS sync origin. Source/build checks do not qualify Android runtime behavior.

authentication.note: Preserve the Better Auth 1.7.12 upgrade, JWT/provider-account migrations, explicit provider linking, nonce validation, verified-email admission and scoped Apple origin checks. Reset atomically consumes its token, writes the password, verifies the mailbox and retires sessions, native authority, access tokens, feeds, passkeys, provider links and pending account proofs while retaining TOTP and backup codes. Enforce the enrolled local factor on every sign-in path, including social/OIDC/SAML callbacks, passkeys and native system-browser flows. Reuse the plugin challenge, provisional-session deletion and reset invalidation. Provider MFA and remembered-device cookies cannot substitute. Native grants retain their ID and stay unapproved until successful factor completion and explicit consent; no bridge permissions or credential formats change. Upgrade server/web together and reload sign-in pages; rollback loses this protection. The password credential remains linked so password-protected account settings keep their password requirement. Other provider accounts can still be unlinked. No credential format or native handoff changes.

compatibility.note: Migration 0092 binds membership-key inserts to the recipient membership and caller granter, restricts wrap and request updates to their writer columns, and guards broad custom grants with triggers. Existing non-superuser roles with DELETE on focus_interval_start retain pruning execution automatically. Startup reports privileged attributes, memberships, RLS ownership and missing cleanup execution; pruning errors do not stop reminder scanning. Deployment logins and Zero publications are unchanged.
compatibility.upgrade: Stop app and Zero writers, back up the coordinated recovery set, and apply 0092 using the migration owner. Existing non-superuser runtime roles with DELETE on focus_interval_start receive cleanup execution during migration, including custom names. Newly created roles or roles without that prior privilege need the documented explicit grant before deployment. Check provider-admin memberships before upgrading.
compatibility.backup: Preserve the existing coordinated PostgreSQL, encrypted attachment, replica and original-secret recovery set. No encrypted-data conversion or row rewrite occurs.
compatibility.rollback: Keep the migration, column grants and function ACL when rolling back the app; the preceding writers use the same wrap and fulfilment columns and pruning function. Restoring the coordinated backup discards newer changes.
compatibility.clientVersions: Existing browser and native clients remain compatible; no client schema or storage format changes.

clients.note: Ship CLI/MCP/TUI JavaScript bundles for user-installed Bun 1.3.14+; document archive/checksum verification, MCP launch, JSON --version, BUILDINFO building-Bun identity, source URLs and notices/license texts covering every bundled or dependency-inlined package. The shebang uses --no-env-file and --config=/dev/null to prevent working-directory environment/preload injection. Minimum-version failure exits 2 and suffixes are tolerated. Scope is any Bun OS, qualified on Linux x64; rebuilds name tagged commit, building Bun and GNU tar. Commands, API envelopes, other exit codes and environment credentials remain unchanged. Standalone binary publication remains blocked/deferred.

public-api.note: Preserve minute, second and fractional-second ISO timestamp acceptance for task create/update/completion, observations and metadata. Offset-capable inputs retain explicit offsets or Z; UTC-only responses remain UTC-only. CSV retains acceptance and normalization. No API version or persisted format changes.
